engineering_decision.rationale: With graph expansion passed both outputs (2 of 2, rubric pass rate 1.0) and met every frozen condition: no blocking failure, question time at most 22.781 s against the 360 s limit, human review 2.0 minutes per output against 10, and 29,409 reported tokens against 200,000. Without graph expansion passed 1 of 2 (rate 0.5) and fails the minimum rate of 1.0: on EC-06-1-v1 only F-1 was supplied, so the explanation could not express the query embedding to embedding model connection, although it contained no unsupported claim. Only with graph expansion qualifies, so the frozen rule permits adoption. The decision covers these two exposed development cases only.
engineering_decision.teaching_prediction_comparison: The observed judgments agree in direction with the teaching comparison: graph expansion adds the F-2 evidence for the second edge where the one-hop path stops at F-1, and the extra evidence made a complete explanation possible. They differ in that the difference appeared on one of two cases only, because on EC-06-2-v1 both configurations supplied F-1 and F-2 and both passed with identical claims; the actual rates (0.5 and 1.0) come from my own judgments, not from the theory's stipulated outputs.
engineering_decision.graph_preparation_trade_off: Coverage gain: the graph path C-RET to C-QUERY to C-MODEL surfaced F-2, which the baseline selection did not admit on EC-06-1-v1. Cost: the graph needed manual review of mentions and relation directions (a rejected reversed proposal and one unresolved mention), compilation and verification, plus continuing maintenance whenever sources change; no preparation timings were measured and none are claimed. In the budget-exclusion probe, expansion also found F-2 but the 250-character budget excluded it, so the coverage gain is not unconditional. Two development cases do not establish a deployment benefit.

scope: These exposed development cases only; no deployment or population-wide claim.
